findings.text: Within the first two sentences a newcomer can say what Athena is and what sets it apart: one model does the work, a second checks it, and cost is recorded. This is a strong opening.
findings.source: header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost."

findings.text: The page says why it exists: the firstmate study is a demonstration of what Athena can do. A newcomer who came for Athena learns why the rest of the page is about a different project.
findings.source: header lede: "Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it with every statement traced to a claim, and every claim to lines in the project's own files."

findings.text: The next step is easy to find and concrete. But the install line assumes the reader has already cloned the repository and gives no clone command, so the first real step means following the GitHub link.
findings.source: header: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself" and Next steps: "Install Athena from a checkout of its repository: ./setup.sh" / "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: This link sits next to the newcomer's next step but is meant for the project owner, and nothing says who "your" refers to. A newcomer may click it and get lost.
findings.source: header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The "Words used first" list leaves out terms the walkthrough uses right away: "place", "capacity", "spawn", "exit 75" and "PR". They are defined only in the Glossary near the end, so a newcomer reading top to bottom hits terms nobody has explained yet.
findings.source: Start here: "If every place of a declared capacity is held, the spawn exits 75 and the item stays queued."

findings.text: The transition cards get dense. "harness", "note", "pin" and "stale wake" come up with no explanation nearby, and "pin" here means something different from the page's own "Pinned firstmate commit". A reader who isn't technical will probably skim this part.
findings.source: t8 card: "A ship or scout keeps its recorded harness and needs a note; a secondmate re-reads its pin and needs none"

findings.text: A newcomer can quickly say what firstmate is, and the eight-step "One piece of work, start to finish" list is a readable path through it. A reader who stops after Start here still comes away with a sound picture.
findings.source: Start here: "Firstmate is a tool that keeps a backlog of programming tasks and hands each one to a separate AI coding tool, called a worker, so that several tasks can run side by side."

findings.text: This section is about how the page was built, not about Athena or firstmate. It doesn't help a newcomer and doesn't say which repository the studies/ folder is in.
findings.source: About this page: "This page's study id, firstmate-work-handling, is the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."
